key: When ONE came into existence, there was ONE, but it was formless. When things got that by which they came into existence, it was called their virtue.
s: A brief account of the beginning moves from the Nameless toward destiny, form and nature; Guo Xiang, on chapter 12, reads it as things getting life of themselves, since non-being cannot produce them, and virtue as leaving them to that self-getting.
src: Guo Xiang, Zhuangzi zhu, chapter 12, zh.wikisource (Nanhua zhenjing zhushu, juan 14, the Zhengtong Daozang edition), revision 6356578 (2026)

evidence.words: 夫一之所起，起於至一，非起於無也。…夫無不能生物，而云物得以生，乃所以明物生之自得，任其自得，斯可謂德也。
evidence.gloss: The arising of the One arises from the utmost One, not from non-being. … Non-being cannot produce things; the text says things got that by which they live to make clear that the life of things is got of themselves, and leaving them to that self-getting may be called virtue.

reason: Key verbatim (verse.js ok, Zhuangzi 12.66, at 1046). Opened the chapter 12 packet: Guo Xiang on 一之所起 says the One arises from the utmost One, not from non-being, and on 物得以生，謂之德 says non-being cannot produce things, the phrase makes clear that things get life of themselves, and leaving them to that self-getting is virtue; the reading paraphrases exactly this. Plain sense faithful to Giles 12.64 to 12.73 (Nothing, the Nameless, ONE, virtue, destiny, form, nature). entry-check ok.
